relevance_note: Case series of three children with HA20 and germline TNFAIP3 variants: "Genetic testing showed that all three patients had heterozygous mutation in TNFAIP3 gene."
method_note: Read the whole paper; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON from my reading and located every quote in the paper (matching its thin/no-break spaces and curly apostrophes so spans are exact). Table 1 has patients as columns (column headers "Patient1", "Patient2", "Patient3"); Table 2 has patients as rows. Table-cell spans were cut from the table lines by script and checked by hand against the tables. INTERPRETATION: Table 1 is a +/– presence table, so "–" was read as explicitly absent (excluded), not as a missing-data dash under rule 6; the text corroborates several of its negatives. The "–" cells in the urine and ANA columns of Table 2 were read the same way (consistent with "The antinuclear antibody (ANA) panel was negative" for Patient 1, normal urine for Patient 2). INDIVIDUALS: 3 patients; Patient 3's mother (carrier, recurrent oral and genital ulcers); and 5 tested parents without a reported variant: Patient 3's father (text: "The father did not carry the mutation") and the parents of Patients 1 and 2, who appear only in figure captions ("Map of gene mutations of Patient 1’s father", etc.) and in Methods ("blood was collected from each child and their parents"). The parents have no variant rows and all-"not reported" checklists. is_proband is null for the 3 patients because the paper never calls them proband/index case and it is not a single-patient report. AGES: only ages at admission are printed (e.g. "A 3 years and 2 months girl was admitted"); I recorded them as age at last evaluation although follow-up continued 3–4 months later; no age at diagnosis is printed. Onset is given only relative to admission (e.g. "Six months before admission"), recorded as text with ISO null (no arithmetic). INHERITANCE: "de novo" for Patients 1 and 2 rests on "confirmed by Sanger sequencing as spontaneous mutations" plus parental sampling; the paper does not literally say each parent tested negative. VARIANT STRINGS: Patient 1's variant is printed "c.925-927dup (p. Val309dup)" in the case text and "c.925_927dup" in the results paragraph; the case-text form is recorded. CONTRADICTIONS/INCONSISTENCIES: (1) Patient 1 sex: "girl"/"her" throughout and Methods "1 male, 2 female" (Patient 3 is the boy), but once "a 91 cm and 11.5 kg boy"; recorded female. (2) Patient 3 CRP: text "CRP of 105 mg/L" vs Table 2 "17.5" prior to treatment. (3) Patient 2: Table 1 "Renal damage +" but "Conventional urine tests and 24-h urinary protein were normal", Table 2 urine "–", and "Renal biopsy was not performed"; both features recorded as separate rows. (4) Patient 2 ANA titre 1:100 and later 1:1000 in text vs 1:320 in Table 2 (possibly different time points). (5) Patient 2 height "105 cm" at examination vs "130 cm at age 11". (6) Patients 1 and 2 have identical local-hospital values (CRP 42.7 mg/L, AESR 50 mm/60 min), a possible copy error. (7) Figure numbering: the text cites Fig. 3 for Patient 2's spine MRI and Figs. 4/5 for the Patient 2/3 gene maps, but the captions label Fig. 3 as Patient 2's gene maps, Fig. 4 as Patient 3's and Fig. 5 as CT/MRI; Fig. 1 is cited for genetic results but captioned as protein domains. Caption images were not used for phenotypes. (8) Follow-up: the abstract says Patients 1 and 2 were followed for four and 3 months; the Patient 1 text says adalimumab for 3 months. TIME-LIMITED NEGATIVES: not emitted when the same feature was later reported present (Patient 1 "no fever" and "no ... bloody stool" at onset; Patient 3 "no ... abdominal pain" at onset). CHECKLIST (D-21, conservative): "Rash –" alone does not exclude the composite skin-lesions item; ANA/ANCA negativity does not exclude "autoantibodies (ANA/other)"; Patient 2's "Gastrointestinal elcer –" plus "no ... gastrointestinal symptoms" leaves "gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation" not reported; "Oculopathy –" (broader) excludes "uveitis or other ocular inflammation"; Patient 3's "arthritis or arthralgia" is excluded because both arthritis (Table 1) and "joint swelling and pain" are negated. No functional assays are reported (only population-database absence, GERP++ conservation and OTU-domain location), so functional evidence is not reported. The Discussion's literature summary (35 patients in 14 families) is aggregate only and gives no per-person rows.
